answers.how: The red ball's diameter is about 62.5 pixels, mapping to 7 cm (scale = 0.112 cm/px). I tracked the ball's position at 0.083s, 0.167s, and 0.250s. Using a quadratic fit on these positions, the velocity components at exactly 0.2s were calculated, yielding a speed of about 339 pixels/s, which converts to 38.0 cm/s.

Using the same scale (1 px = 0.112 cm), I tracked the ball around 0.6s (frames at 0.500s, 0.583s, and 0.667s). A quadratic interpolation gives the instantaneous velocity at 0.6s as approximately 583 pixels/s. Converting this with the scale gives 65.3 cm/s.

From the quadratic fit of the trajectory between 0.083s and 0.250s (during the bounce at the end of the stem), the constant acceleration in this interval is approximately 8352 pixels/s^2 directed upwards. Multiplying by the 0.112 cm/px scale yields 935.4 cm/s^2.
